terminology.filter: operation or learned detector when qualified
terminology.cross-correlation: unflipped operation commonly implemented by libraries
terminology.receptive field: input region that may affect an activation

records.definition: A local weighted sum with the kernel reversed.
records.technical: Each output coordinate aggregates a translated patch.
records.algorithm: flip kernel; multiply matching entries; sum.
records.implementation: Most ML APIs use correlation instead; state convention.
records.engineering: Boundary extension and layout change results.
records.limitations: Finite borders violate ideal translation behavior.

records.definition: Sliding dot product without reversing the kernel.
records.intuition: Compare one local patch to one pattern.
records.engineering: Name convention in reviews and reproductions.
records.example: identity leaves valid patch centers unchanged.
records.limitations: Not the normalized statistical correlation coefficient.
misconceptions: identical to convolution for all kernels

records.definition: Finite coefficients applied to each local neighborhood.
records.technical: A CNN weight tensor has output-, input-channel, height, width axes.
records.math: K in R^(Cout x Cin x kh x kw)
records.algorithm: one dot product per placement and output channel.
records.implementation: Validate finite values and compatible channels.
records.engineering: More coefficients increase cost and capacity.
records.limitations: A kernel need not be learned.

records.definition: Values supplied beyond an input boundary.
records.intuition: Lets a kernel center visit edge pixels.
records.technical: Policy and amount determine border responses and shape.
records.implementation: Record zero, reflect, or replicate policy.
records.engineering: Zero padding may create artificial edges.

records.technical: Stride greater than one reduces spatial sampling.
records.engineering: It saves compute but may alias or skip detail.

records.technical: It expands effective kernel support without adding weights.

records.definition: Output activations produced by one filter.
records.intuition: A map of where a detector responds.
records.technical: One output channel is one spatial response plane.
records.math: Y in R^(N x Cout x Hout x Wout)

records.definition: Input region that can influence an activation.
records.engineering: Effective influence can be smaller than theoretical.
misconceptions: it is one fixed input pixel

records.definition: Indexed tensor dimension for measurements or responses.
records.math: x in R^(Cin x H x W)
records.algorithm: accumulate across Cin per output channel.
records.engineering: More channels cost memory and compute.
records.limitations: A channel is not inherently interpretable.

records.definition: A kernel optimized from data and an objective.
records.intuition: A detector adjusted by gradient feedback.
records.technical: Weights receive gradients through the loss.
records.engineering: Patterns depend on data, objective, and regularization.

records.definition: A translated input yields a correspondingly translated output.
records.intuition: Move the pattern; move its response.
records.technical: Approximate for finite images; stride and padding break exact behavior.
records.limitations: CNNs are not fully translation invariant.
